newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello rules against CanWest stake in Ten.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello rules against CanWest stake in Ten.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday he had ruled that CanWest Global Communication Corp's increased economic interest in Ten Group Ltd was inconsistent with foreign investment policy.

"The Treasurer has ruled that the increase in the economic interest by Canadian company CanWest Global Communications Corp in the Ten Group Ltd (TGL) is inconsistent with the government's foreign investment policy," Costello said in a statement.
Costello said Canwest must sell its current 76 percent economic interst down to the previously sanctioned 57.5 percent.
Costello shares held in Ten by CanWest associates Selli Pty Ltd, Numeration Pty Ltd, Turnand Pty Ltd and Donholken Pty Ltd would need to be sold by September 30 "irrespective of price."

"These shares can only be sold to a person or persons approved in writing by the Treasurer and CanWest must provide a statuatory declaration to the effect that they have no linkages with the new shareholders," Costello said.

He said this would have the effect of returning CanWest's holding to its level of November 1995 when the Australian Broadcasting Authority ruled that CanWest did not control Ten even though it held an economic interest of 57.5 percent.

Under Australian foreign investment rules, foreign investors may not control or hold no more than a 15 percent voting interest in an Australian broadcaster and total foreign holding must not exceed 20 percent.
CanWest says it meets this requirement by voting only 15 percent of its stake in the unlisted broadcaster.
Costello said the government would have to be satisfied that foreign investment rules were being met before it would consider any proposal for foreign investment in a proposed float of Ten.

"In addition, acceptance of CanWest continuing to have a 57.5 percent interest in (Ten) prior prior to the float would be entirely without prejudice to the government's views on the ownership parameters for a floated (Ten)," he said.
Costello said the government has advised CanWest of its decision. "Further contact with relevant parties is underway in relation to the implementation of the government's decisions," Costello said.

Canwest said early in April that it was exploring its options after the Australian Broadcasting Authority ruled that Canwest was in breach of foreign ownership rules in connection with CanWest's control of Australia's Ten television network.
The Australian Financial Review reported earlier on Friday that Canwest had offered to sell down its stake in Ten to 57.5 percent, provided its holding is protected at that level.
